subQuestions.questionText: What is the NAME of the functional group of an ALDEHYDE?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The aldehyde functional group (–CHO) is called the formyl group.

subQuestions.questionText: Which test would IDENTIFY an UNSATURATED compound?

options.A: Add NaOH — if neutralisation occurs it is unsaturated
options.B: Test with litmus — unsaturated compounds turn litmus red
options.D: Burn — unsaturated compounds produce a blue flame

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Unsaturated compounds (with C=C or C≡C) decolourise bromine water via addition. Orange/brown Br₂ becomes colourless.

subQuestions.questionText: What is the EMPIRICAL FORMULA of ethyl ethanoate (C₄H₈O₂)?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Simplify C₄H₈O₂ by dividing by 2: C₂H₄O.

subQuestions.questionText:
10 g of CaCO₃ is reacted with excess HCl. This is compared to a previous experiment (Curve P) using 5 g of CaCO₃. Which curve describes the new experiment?

*(Refer to the graph in the original question paper.)*

options.A: Curve I — same rate, same total volume
options.B: Curve II — higher rate, same total volume
options.C: Curve III — same initial rate, higher total volume
options.D: Curve IV — higher rate, higher total volume

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Same concentration of HCl (excess) so same initial rate. But 10g CaCO₃ = double the limiting reagent → double total CO₂ produced → higher plateau. Same initial gradient, higher final volume → Curve III.

subQuestions.questionText:
HCl is added to the CrO₄²⁻/Cr₂O₇²⁻ equilibrium: 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O. Which statements are TRUE?

(i) The colour changes from yellow to orange.
(ii) The forward reaction is favoured.
(iii) Kc changes when HCl is added.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D (2 marks) per summary. Adding HCl increases [H⁺] → forward reaction favoured (ii true) → more Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) produced (i true). Kc only changes with temperature, NOT with concentration change (iii false). Reconsider: answer D (ii) and (iii) — if Kc does change... No. Kc is constant at constant T. Accept per exam memo.

subQuestions.questionText: For the equilibrium A(g) + B(g) ⇌ C(g) + D(g), Kc = 1 × 10⁻⁴. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.A: Equilibrium lies far to the right; [C][D] >> [A][B]
options.C: Equal amounts of products and reactants are present
options.D: The reaction does not reach equilibrium

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Kc = [C][D]/[A][B] = 1×10⁻⁴ (very small). Very small Kc means equilibrium lies far to the LEFT → much more reactants than products → [A][B] >> [C][D].

subQuestions.questionText: Oxalic acid (H₂C₂O₄) reacts with NaOH. Which equation is CORRECT?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
H₂C₂O₄ is a diprotic acid. Full neutralisation: H₂C₂O₄ + 2NaOH → (COO⁻)₂Na₂ + 2H₂O = Na₂C₂O₄ + 2H₂O.

subQuestions.questionText: Which acid is the WEAKEST? (Ka values: A = 4.5×10⁻⁶, B = 1.8×10⁻⁵, C = 6.3×10⁻⁵, D = 4.5×10⁻⁴)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Weaker acid = smaller Ka (less ionisation). Ka = 4.5×10⁻⁶ is the smallest.

subQuestions.questionText: In the purification of copper by electrolysis, which ONE is CORRECT?

options.A: Cathode mass decreases; anode mass increases
options.B: Anode mass decreases; cathode mass increases; solution colour unchanged

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Pure copper is deposited at cathode (mass increases). Impure copper anode dissolves (mass decreases). [Cu²⁺] stays approximately constant → solution colour (blue) unchanged.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following represents a SPONTANEOUS REDOX reaction?

options.C: Zn + 2H⁺ → Zn²⁺ + H₂ only when heated

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Spontaneous if E°_cell > 0. E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V, E°(I₂/I⁻) = +0.54 V. Cell: Fe³⁺ reduced (cathode), I⁻ oxidised (anode). E°_cell = 0.77 − 0.54 = +0.23 V > 0 → spontaneous.

subQuestions.questionText: Define HYDROCARBON.
subQuestions.memoText: A hydrocarbon is an organic compound that contains ONLY carbon and hydrogen atoms. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: From the list of compounds A–H, identify TWO UNSATURATED HYDROCARBONS.
subQuestions.memoText: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain C=C or C≡C bonds AND only C and H. Identify TWO such compounds from the given structures. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO compounds that are CHAIN ISOMERS of each other.
subQuestions.memoText: Chain isomers: same molecular formula, same functional group type, different carbon skeleton. Identify the pair. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which compound is a SECONDARY ALCOHOL?
subQuestions.memoText: Secondary alcohol: –OH group attached to a carbon bonded to two other carbon atoms (not at the end of the chain). Identify from structures. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the STRUCTURAL FORMULA of a FUNCTIONAL ISOMER of compound D.
subQuestions.memoText: Functional isomers: same molecular formula, different functional group. If D is a carboxylic acid, a functional isomer is an ester with same formula. Draw structural formula. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the GENERAL FORMULA of the homologous series to which compound B belongs.
subQuestions.memoText: Identify the homologous series of B and give its general formula (e.g., CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ for alkenes, CₙH₂ₙO for aldehydes/ketones, etc.). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the STRUCTURAL FORMULA of compound C (3-ethylpent-1-yne).
subQuestions.memoText: 3-ethylpent-1-yne: HC≡C–CH(C₂H₅)–CH₂–CH₃. Main chain = 5 carbons. Triple bond C1–C2. Ethyl group on C3. Draw all bonds. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound E.
subQuestions.memoText: Apply IUPAC rules to structure E in the original paper. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound G.
subQuestions.memoText: Apply IUPAC rules to structure G. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound H.
subQuestions.memoText: Apply IUPAC rules to structure H. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Write a BALANCED EQUATION for the COMPLETE COMBUSTION of compound B (using molecular formulae).
subQuestions.memoText: General combustion: CₙHₘ + (n + m/4)O₂ → nCO₂ + (m/2)H₂O. Substitute the molecular formula of B and balance. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Define BOILING POINT.
subQuestions.memoText: The boiling point is the temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid equals the external (atmospheric) pressure. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which compound is a LIQUID at 100°C? (Given: A bp = 78°C, B bp = 46°C, C alcohol bp = 118°C, D aldehyde bp = X°C.)
subQuestions.memoText: Compound A (bp = 78°C < 100°C) — wait: if bp = 78°C, it boils below 100°C so it is a GAS at 100°C. Compound C (bp = 118°C > 100°C) is a LIQUID at 100°C. Answer: A or C depending on which has bp > 100°C. Accept C (alcohol, bp = 118°C > 100°C → liquid at 100°C). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the DIFFERENCE in boiling points between compound A (78°C) and compound B (46°C).
subQuestions.memoText: Both are haloalkanes (or given compounds). Higher molecular mass / longer chain / more electrons in A → stronger London dispersion forces → higher boiling point. OR if different functional groups: explain in terms of type and strength of IMFs. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Estimate the VALUE of X (boiling point of aldehyde D) from the data.
subQuestions.memoText: Aldehyde D: dipole-dipole forces (no H-bonding). Expected lower bp than alcohol C (118°C) but higher than alkane of similar mass. From typical values or interpolation from given data, state X. (1 mark — accept reading from graph.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain your value of X in terms of INTERMOLECULAR FORCES compared to alcohol C.
subQuestions.memoText: Aldehyde D has dipole-dipole forces (polar C=O but no O–H). Alcohol C has hydrogen bonding (stronger than dipole-dipole). Hydrogen bonds require more energy to break → C has higher bp. Aldehyde D has lower bp (X < 118°C). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the EFFECT on the boiling points of all compounds if the external pressure is LOWERED?
subQuestions.memoText: Boiling points DECREASE. At lower external pressure, vapour pressure equals atmospheric pressure at a lower temperature → substance boils at lower temperature. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In the esterification of methanol with propanoic acid, what is the CATALYST?
subQuestions.memoText: Concentrated sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What TYPE of reaction is esterification?
subQuestions.memoText: Condensation reaction (also accept: esterification). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why a WATER BATH is used instead of direct heating in the esterification experiment.
subQuestions.memoText: (1) The reactants/products are flammable (volatile organic compounds) — water bath provides gentle, even heating and reduces fire risk. (2) Water bath provides more controlled/uniform temperature to prevent overheating/boiling. (2 marks — any two valid reasons.)

subQuestions.questionText: Write a BALANCED EQUATION using STRUCTURAL FORMULAE for the esterification of methanol with propanoic acid.
subQuestions.memoText: CH₃OH + CH₃CH₂COOH ⇌ CH₃OOCCH₂CH₃ + H₂O. Draw all structural formulae explicitly. Methanol + propanoic acid → methyl propanoate + water. (5 marks: structures, arrow, product, water.)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of the ester product.
subQuestions.memoText: Methyl propanoate. (Methanol provides the methyl group; propanoic acid provides the propanoate.) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: In the flow diagram, state the INORGANIC REACTANT in Reaction 2.
subQuestions.memoText: HBr (or HCl or Br₂ depending on context of reaction 2). State the specific inorganic reagent shown in the flow diagram. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound B in the flow diagram.
subQuestions.memoText: Name compound B using IUPAC rules based on its structure in the diagram. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What TYPE of reaction is Reaction 1?
subQuestions.memoText: Identify type: addition, substitution, elimination, esterification, hydrogenation, etc. based on reactants and products in the flow diagram. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the CATALYST for Reaction 3.
subQuestions.memoText: Concentrated H₂SO₄ (for dehydration/esterification) OR V₂O₅ (for oxidation) OR another catalyst as shown. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the IUPAC NAME of compound D in the flow diagram.
subQuestions.memoText: Name compound D using IUPAC rules. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What TYPE of reaction is Reaction 3?
subQuestions.memoText: State the reaction type: addition/substitution/elimination/esterification/cracking/hydrogenation. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What TYPE of haloalkane is compound A?
subQuestions.memoText: Primary/secondary/tertiary haloalkane — based on the carbon bearing the halogen and how many carbons are bonded to it. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From energy Diagram A, is the reaction 2Al + 3H₂SO₄ → Al₂(SO₄)₃ + 3H₂ EXOTHERMIC or ENDOTHERMIC? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: EXOTHERMIC. The products are at a lower energy level than the reactants (from Diagram A, product energy < reactant energy). Energy is released. ΔH < 0. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What does the SHADED AREA in energy Diagram A represent?
subQuestions.memoText: The shaded area represents the ACTIVATION ENERGY (Ea) — the minimum energy required for the reaction to occur / the energy barrier. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From the energy diagram, determine the VALUE of X (activation energy for forward reaction without catalyst). Values given: 240.8, 217.3, 208.2, 86.5 kJ.
subQuestions.memoText: X = activation energy (without catalyst) = height of activated complex above reactants. From given values: X = 240.8 − (reactant energy). Identify reactant and activated complex levels. (2 marks — read from diagram.)

subQuestions.questionText: In the Maxwell-Boltzmann Diagram B at 30°C, what does the SHADED AREA represent?
subQuestions.memoText: The shaded area represents the fraction of molecules with kinetic energy ≥ activation energy Ea (molecules that have sufficient energy to react). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the VALUE of Y (the activation energy) at 30°C?
subQuestions.memoText: Y = Ea = same as X from Diagram A (temperature doesn't change activation energy). Read from diagram. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the TOTAL VOLUME of H₂ produced when all Al reacts?
subQuestions.memoText: From stoichiometry: 2Al + 3H₂SO₄ → 3H₂. n(H₂) = (3/2) × n(Al). Volume = n(H₂) × molar volume. (1 mark — read from graph maximum.)

subQuestions.questionText: What is the INDEPENDENT VARIABLE in the investigation comparing different particle sizes of Al?
subQuestions.memoText: Particle size of aluminium (surface area). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Use COLLISION THEORY to explain why smaller Al particles react faster with H₂SO₄.
subQuestions.memoText: Smaller particles → greater total surface area exposed. More surface area → more contact between Al atoms and H₂SO₄ molecules. More collisions per unit time between reactant particles. More effective (successful) collisions per unit time → higher reaction rate. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: In RUN 3: reaction complete at t = 2.6 min, average rate = 40 cm³/s, Vm = 27 000 cm³/mol. Calculate the PERCENTAGE PURITY of the Al sample.
subQuestions.memoText: Total H₂ = rate × time = 40 × (2.6 × 60) = 40 × 156 = 6240 cm³. Moles H₂ = 6240/27000 = 0.2311 mol. Moles Al (pure) = (2/3) × 0.2311 = 0.1541 mol. Mass pure Al = 0.1541 × 27 = 4.16 g. % purity = (4.16/mass of sample) × 100. (6 marks — need sample mass from question data.)

subQuestions.questionText: State LE CHATELIER'S PRINCIPLE.
subQuestions.memoText: When an equilibrium is disturbed by a change in conditions, the system will respond to counteract the change and re-establish equilibrium. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The concentration-time graphs A (298 K) and B (398 K) show parallel lines for P₂Q. What do the PARALLEL LINES mean?
subQuestions.memoText: The concentrations of the species change at the same rate / both lines have the same slope. This means the STOICHIOMETRIC RATIO is maintained — the rate of change of each species is proportional to its stoichiometric coefficient. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Is the reaction P₂Q(g) + 3Q(s) ⇌ 2PQ₂(g) EXOTHERMIC or ENDOTHERMIC?
subQuestions.memoText: From graphs: at higher temperature (398 K vs 298 K), if Kc increases → endothermic. If Kc decreases → exothermic. Read from graph B vs A. (1 mark — answer depends on graph.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain your answer to 6.3 using Le Chatelier's principle.
subQuestions.memoText: If endothermic: increasing T provides energy → system absorbs energy by shifting forward → more PQ₂, less P₂Q → Kc increases. If exothermic: reverse argument. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Is Kc at graph B (398 K) GREATER THAN, EQUAL TO or LESS THAN Kc at graph A (298 K)?
subQuestions.memoText: Compare equilibrium concentrations at the two temperatures. State which Kc is larger based on graph. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: At 398 K (Kc = 0.49), [PQ₂] = 0.35 mol/dm³ at equilibrium. The volume is 1 dm³. Calculate the INITIAL MOLES of P₂Q.
subQuestions.memoText: P₂Q(g) + 3Q(s) ⇌ 2PQ₂(g). Q is solid → excluded from Kc. Kc = [PQ₂]²/[P₂Q] = 0.49. 0.35² / [P₂Q] = 0.49. [P₂Q]_eq = 0.1225/0.49 = 0.25 mol/dm³. ICE: initial [P₂Q] = x, change = −0.175 (since [PQ₂] = 0.35, Δ[PQ₂] = 0.35, so Δ[P₂Q] = 0.35/2 = 0.175). x − 0.175 = 0.25. x = 0.425 mol/dm³. In 1 dm³: initial moles P₂Q = 0.425 mol. (8 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: At t = 8 min, describe the CHANGE made to the system based on the graph.
subQuestions.memoText: Read from graph: at t = 8 min, a sudden change in concentration is visible (e.g., increase or decrease in [P₂Q] or [PQ₂]). Describe: reactant/product added, or volume changed, etc. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the change at t = 8 min using Le Chatelier's principle.
subQuestions.memoText: Based on what changed at t = 8 min: state how the system responds to oppose the change, which direction equilibrium shifts, and how concentrations adjust. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: 10 g of Na₂CO₃ is dissolved in 0.7 dm³ of solution. Calculate the CONCENTRATION of Na₂CO₃.
Is the pH of the Na₂CO₃ solution GREATER THAN or LESS THAN 7?
subQuestions.memoText: GREATER THAN 7. Na₂CO₃ is the salt of a strong base (NaOH) and weak acid (H₂CO₃) → the solution is ALKALINE → pH > 7. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write an EQUATION to explain the pH of the Na₂CO₃ solution.
subQuestions.memoText: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ (hydrolysis of carbonate ion produces OH⁻ → alkaline). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which INDICATOR would be BEST for a titration of Na₂CO₃ with HCl? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: Methyl orange (changes colour at pH 3.1–4.4) is suitable for strong acid–weak base titrations (equivalence point pH < 7). Alternatively phenolphthalein if only first equivalence point (to NaHCO₃). (2 marks — methyl orange with reason.)

subQuestions.questionText: Define DILUTE ACID.
subQuestions.memoText: A dilute acid is an acid dissolved in a large amount of water / an acid with a low concentration of H⁺ ions (small amount of acid per volume of solution). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: 0.01 mol H₂SO₄ and 0.024 mol KOH are mixed in a 0.2 dm³ solution. Calculate the pH of the final solution.
subQuestions.memoText: H₂SO₄ + 2KOH → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles H⁺ from H₂SO₄ = 2 × 0.01 = 0.02 mol. Moles OH⁻ from KOH = 0.024 mol. Excess OH⁻ = 0.024 − 0.02 = 0.004 mol. [OH⁻] = 0.004/0.2 = 0.02 mol/dm³. pOH = −log(0.02) = 1.699. pH = 14 − 1.699 = 12.3. (8 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: In the cell Al|Al³⁺ || M²⁺|M, which species is the REDUCING AGENT?
subQuestions.memoText: Al (aluminium) is the reducing agent — it is oxidised at the anode (loses electrons). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: From the emf vs [M²⁺] graph, determine [M²⁺] when emf = 1.87 V.
subQuestions.memoText: Read from graph at emf = 1.87 V: [M²⁺] = (value from graph). (2 marks — graphical reading.)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe HOW [M²⁺] changes as the cell operates. Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: [M²⁺] INCREASES as cell operates. At the cathode: M²⁺ + 2e⁻ → M (M²⁺ consumed). Wait: if M is cathode: M²⁺ is reduced → [M²⁺] decreases. OR at anode: Al → Al³⁺ + 3e⁻. For Al|Al³⁺ || M²⁺|M: cathode is M side. M²⁺ is reduced → [M²⁺] DECREASES. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: In which direction do K⁺ ions in the salt bridge move during operation?
subQuestions.memoText: K⁺ ions move towards the Al|Al³⁺ half-cell (anode compartment) to maintain electrical neutrality (Al³⁺ is produced, making solution positive → K⁺ moves away from cathode, towards anode). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: IDENTIFY metal M from the emf vs [M²⁺] graph. (E°(Al³⁺/Al) = −1.66 V; read E°_cell at standard [M²⁺] = 1 mol/dm³ from graph ≈ 1.80 V.)
subQuestions.memoText: E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode. 1.80 = E°_M − (−1.66). E°_M = 1.80 − 1.66 = 0.14 V. From table: E°(Sn²⁺/Sn) = +0.14 V. M = Tin (Sn). (6 marks: read from graph, apply formula, identify.)

subQuestions.questionText: If M is replaced by Mg, which electrode will be the ANODE?
subQuestions.memoText: Al electrode (anode). E°(Mg²⁺/Mg) = −2.37 V vs E°(Al³⁺/Al) = −1.66 V. Mg is stronger reducing agent (more negative E°) → Mg would be oxidised (anode). But cell is Al|Al³⁺ || Mg²⁺|Mg... If Mg has lower E°, Mg is anode. Reconsider: which is anode in Al vs Mg cell? Mg (−2.37 V) is stronger reducing agent → Mg is anode. BUT the cell notation is fixed with Al on left. If Mg replaces M (which was Sn at cathode), new cell: Al vs Mg. Mg is stronger reducing agent → Mg is oxidised → Mg is anode. Al is cathode? No — Al (−1.66 V) > Mg (−2.37 V) → Al is cathode, Mg is anode. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain using OXIDISING AGENT strength why the chosen electrode is the anode.
subQuestions.memoText: Al³⁺ (E° = −1.66 V) is a stronger oxidising agent than Mg²⁺ (E° = −2.37 V). Al³⁺ is more readily reduced. Therefore Mg is the stronger reducing agent and will be oxidised (anode). The electrode that is the stronger reducing agent is the anode. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the ENERGY CONVERSION in the silver electroplating cell.
subQuestions.memoText: Electrical energy is converted to chemical energy. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which terminal (P or Q) of the battery is NEGATIVE?
subQuestions.memoText: The terminal connected to the CATHODE (object being plated / silver ornament) is negative (P or Q depending on diagram). Cathode is negative in electrolytic cell — connected to negative terminal. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Write the HALF-REACTION at the CATHODE (silver ornament).
subQuestions.memoText: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag (silver ions from solution are reduced and deposited on the ornament). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the CURRENT needed to deposit 3.25 g of silver on the ornament in 30 minutes.
